content:
Out of curiosity, I'm trying to understand what exactly is going on in the soundness bug that was fixed by https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/14807/. This is my attempt: https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/6035570. I have two questions:

  • The AI-generated proof of False uses reflection APIs to build terms and pass them to the kernel directly. I wasn't able to get a more human-readable proof of False that sticks to the normal surface syntax. Why does my attempt fail and is that possible?
  • The exploit relies on the fact that while Lean checks the sort of an inductive type at declaration type, it does not appear to be stored as a universe level but rather the term is re-checked later, possibly after substitutions from specializing to parameters and indices. Not being familiar with the Lean implementation at all, I'm left vaguely wondering if this can be exploited in different ways. For example, it seems to me that generation of recursors looks inside the constructors to see which arguments can be parameters and which must be indices, right? Couldn't there be trouble if a substitution makes it impossible to see that an argument can be a parameter so that in the generated recursor it suddenly becomes an index? Has this sort of question been accounted for?
You may be interested in the discussion at #lean4lean > Successes , which contains a link to another proof of False using the soundness bug.
